Assessment criteria: Customer-relevant three Whys/PBOs; stakeholder and readiness gaps explicit.
Strong / full-credit anchor: Clear hypothesis tied to scenario evidence; all critical roles and go/narrow logic included.
Developing / partial-credit anchor: Mostly relevant but one noncritical readiness or stakeholder gap.
Insufficient / low-credit anchor: Generic pitch, unsupported customer facts or no readiness review.

Assessment criteria: Consultative opening, diagnostic questions, balanced participation and timed convergence.
Strong / full-credit anchor: Outcome-led, non-leading, captures evidence and obtains next-step agreement.
Developing / partial-credit anchor: Adequate structure; weak probing or minor timing imbalance.
Insufficient / low-credit anchor: Product tour or unbounded brainstorming with no customer evidence.

Assessment criteria: Specific workflows, evidence-based impact/effort, first wave and deferral rationale.
Strong / full-credit anchor: Priorities defensible; business/technical owners, dependencies and metric plan present.
Developing / partial-credit anchor: Priorities plausible but incomplete rationale/owners for one case.
Insufficient / low-credit anchor: All ideas marked quick wins or major blockers ignored.

Assessment criteria: Actors, steps, systems, active versus elapsed time, frequency and evidence labels.
Strong / full-credit anchor: Two detailed traceable maps with no unit confusion and honest gaps.
Developing / partial-credit anchor: Two maps with minor missing detail but sound time basis.
Insufficient / low-credit anchor: Missing map, invented baseline or conflated wait and labor.

Assessment criteria: Credible future change, data/access dependencies, human review and exceptions.
Strong / full-credit anchor: Two feasible hypothesis maps; retained controls and reviewed corrections.
Developing / partial-credit anchor: Plausible maps with one noncritical unverified dependency clearly flagged.
Insufficient / low-credit anchor: Unsupported automation, removed essential controls or hidden access risks.

Assessment criteria: Reproducible units, ranges, costs, recapture and evidence; no double counting.
Strong / full-credit anchor: All material assumptions traceable; downside visible; benefit type and sensitivity explained.
Developing / partial-credit anchor: Model mostly correct with fixable documentation or minor nonmaterial error.
Insufficient / low-credit anchor: Material formula/unit error, guaranteed ROI, invented evidence or capacity claimed as cash.

Assessment criteria: Problem → workflow → value/evidence → criteria → decision and sponsor commitments.
Strong / full-credit anchor: Concise decision-led narrative, credible challenge handling and conditional decisions captured.
Developing / partial-credit anchor: Understandable but weak prioritization or one missing noncritical commitment.
Insufficient / low-credit anchor: Generic demo, misleading claims or no decision request.

Assessment criteria: Lightest sufficient validation, alternatives, readiness/approval distinction, owners and dates.
Strong / full-credit anchor: Recommendation fits unresolved question; stop rules and agreed/proposed dates clear.
Developing / partial-credit anchor: Reasonable path with minor sequencing or documentation gap.
Insufficient / low-credit anchor: Unqualified pilot promise, absent criteria or no accountable action plan.

Assessment criteria: Receiving-owner needs, evidence/source traceability, clearance and human accountability.
Strong / full-credit anchor: Complete versioned manifest, risks/exclusions and source/AI review record.
Developing / partial-credit anchor: Usable pack with minor indexing or version gap.
Insufficient / low-credit anchor: Core artifacts missing, confidential data exposed or AI treated as approver.

Dimension: Proposed: ≥80/100 and every critical gate Passed; all dimensions must be scored.
